column_lineage.transformation: DATEDIFF(DAY, CAST(c.reported_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(CAST('2025-12-31' AS DATE) AS DATETIME2))

summary: Nightly staging job J05 extracts active claims from `dbo.claims` into `stg.claims`, excluding rejected claims and computing `claim_age_days` relative to a static as-of date (2025-12-31).
risk_notes: String Collation/Case Sensitivity: T-SQL `c.status <> 'REJECTED'` is case-insensitive by default, whereas PySpark equality checks are case-sensitive. Lowercase or titlecase values like 'rejected' will incorrectly pass through in PySpark unless normalized using `upper(col('status')) != 'REJECTED'`.

Date Function Parameter Order: T-SQL `DATEDIFF(DAY, start, end)` takes the start date (`reported_date`) before the end date (`@asof`). PySpark `datediff(end, start)` expects the end date first (`datediff(lit('2025-12-31'), col('reported_date'))`); reversing them yields negative day counts.

NULL Handling in Filtering: In T-SQL, `status <> 'REJECTED'` evaluates to UNKNOWN and excludes `NULL` values. While PySpark's `filter(col('status') != 'REJECTED')` also drops NULLs, explicit null handling should be confirmed to prevent unintended record loss if `status` can be NULL.

Hardcoded Parameter: The `@asof` variable is hardcoded to '2025-12-31'. Translating this without a parameterized workflow mechanism (e.g., Airflow/Databricks job parameters) will cause static age calculations in production.
